target_customer: Banks, fintechs, brokers and other regulated financial entities in Latin America (later also the US) that must run KYC, KYB and AML checks
problem: Financial entities do compliance onboarding, screening, risk rating and reporting by hand across many tools, which is slow and error prone.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for compliance workflows, with AI agents added later
product_category: Regtech: KYC/KYB, AML monitoring and compliance workflow automation

founders.name: Lucas Ranallo
prior_employers: Family brokerage firm (worked there while building the company)
education: Industrial engineer (degree stated, school not stated)
previous_startups: 3D printer venture with his co-founders, about three years, described as failed
founders.background_notes: Source: Forbes Argentina profile. YC page lists him as founder.

founders.name: Mathias Caramutti
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and in Forbes Argentina and LatamList. Education and employers not found.

founders.name: Bernardo Michel
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CTO by Forbes Argentina; LatamList spells the surname Michell. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Truora
competitors.what: Colombian identity verification, background checks and WhatsApp onboarding for Latin American companies
competitors.traction_then: Over 400 clients in nine countries per April 2022 coverage
competitors.funding_then: Seed of 3.5M USD earlier, then 15M USD Series A announced April 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: Workflow software integrating screening lists, document checks and regulator reporting across several countries. Standard engineering with hard integration and regulatory-detail work.

defensibility.rationale: Compliance workflows embed in a customer's onboarding process and encode local rules, which raises switching costs, but identity vendors could add similar modules.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. The company kept growing independently and stated 130 customers in 10 countries on its own site.

market_need_then: LatAm had more than 2,000 fintechs and about 1,000 traditional financial entities needing KYC and AML processes, per the company's claims in Bloomberg Linea in December 2022.

identity.mascot_or_character: Named AI agents on the site: Screena, Trixie, Kayce, Edd, Audie
identity.voice_and_tone: Professional regtech, product claims about frictionless compliance

rebrands.why: Not stated in sources found. A directory page says Complif was formerly Celeri; 2022 and January 2023 press still used Celeri.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself found; the name Complif is close to unrelated names such as Complii and Cimplifi in search, but no evidence it hurt sales.

pivots.from: 3D printer hardware venture by the same founders
pivots.why: Ranallo saw heavy manual work in financial firms, per Forbes Argentina

outcome_analysis: Complif started as Celeri, sold compliance automation to LatAm financial entities, raised a 2.6M USD seed in late 2022 and by its own account reached 130 customers across 10 countries with AI agents. No Series A was found. It is active, so no failure story applies, and the main open question is whether it can expand beyond LatAm into the US market it now targets.
notes: Aggregators disagree on totals (CB Insights 4.1M, Caplight 5.7M, a pre-seed of 500K in December 2021 on Bouncewatch); these are unverified and not recorded, except the YC 500K stated by Forbes Argentina. Seed date: Bloomberg Linea reported 2.6M on 2022-12-13 and LatamList gave investors on 2023-01-11. Stage seed is from LatamList. No outcome search hits for shutdown, acquisition or layoffs. Founding year 2021 follows Forbes Argentina (launched 2021); LatamList says early 2022. Truora's Series A source is dated April 2022, a few months after the January 2022 as_of.
